lessons.title: Your first print
lessons.objective: Use print() to show text on the screen.

steps.text: Computers follow instructions exactly. print() shows whatever is inside the brackets. Text goes inside quote marks. Press Run!
What will this print?
steps.explanation: print() shows the text inside the quotes. The quote marks themselves are not printed.

steps.text: Each print() starts a new line. Run this to see two lines.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: Every print() puts its text on its own line, so "Nasi" and "lemak" are on two lines.

steps.text: This code has a bug. Fix line 1 so it prints Hello.
steps.hint: Text needs a quote mark at the start AND at the end.
steps.explanation: A string must be closed with a second quote mark: "Hello".

steps.text: Your turn! Write one line that prints: I love coding
steps.hint: Use print() with the words inside quote marks.

lessons.title: Playing with text
lessons.objective: Join text with + and repeat it with *.

steps.text: The + sign joins two pieces of text together. Notice the space inside "Hello, ".
What will this print?
steps.explanation: + glues the two strings together with nothing in between, so you get catfish.

steps.text: The * sign repeats text a number of times.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: "Go! " repeated twice is "Go! Go! ".

steps.text: Python is fussy about capital letters. Fix line 1.
steps.hint: Python commands are written in small letters.
steps.explanation: Python only knows print with a small p. Print with a capital P is a different, unknown name.

steps.text: Join "Hari " and "Raya" with + so it prints: Hari Raya
steps.hint: Put both pieces of text inside print() with a + between them.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.objective: Store values in variables and use them later.

steps.text: A variable is a labelled box that keeps a value. = puts a value into the box.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: Quote marks make "city" plain text, so Python prints the word city, not the variable.

steps.text: A variable can change. The newest value wins.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: food first holds "roti", then is changed to "satay", so satay is printed.

steps.text: Line 2 has a typo in the variable name. Fix it.
steps.hint: Check the spelling of the variable on line 1.
steps.explanation: The variable is called name. nam is a different name Python has never seen.

steps.text: Finish the program so it prints: My pet is a cat
steps.solution:
pet = "cat"
print("My pet is a " + pet)
steps.hint: Join "My pet is a " and the variable pet with +.

lessons.title: Putting it together
lessons.objective: Combine text and variables to make messages.

steps.text: Join variables and text to build a full name. The " " adds a space.
Careful! These numbers are inside quotes. What will this print?
steps.explanation: With quotes they are text, and + joins text, so "1" + "2" makes 12.

steps.text: A comma in print() also joins things, and adds a space for you.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: The comma prints both values with one space between them.

steps.text: Line 2 is missing something between the text and the variable. Fix it.
steps.hint: Use + (or a comma) to join two things.
steps.explanation: Python needs a + or a comma between "Hello " and friend to know they belong together.

steps.text: Finish the program so it prints: Welcome to Melaka!
steps.hint: Join three things: "Welcome to ", town and "!".

lessons.title: Maths with code
lessons.objective: Calculate with + - * / and see the results.

steps.text: Python is a great calculator. / divides and always gives a decimal answer.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: Multiplication happens first: 3 * 4 is 12, then 12 - 2 is 10.

steps.text: // divides and drops the decimal part. % gives the remainder.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.code:
cakes = 20
friends = 6
print(cakes // friends)
print(cakes % friends)
steps.explanation: 20 cakes shared by 6 friends: each gets 3, and 2 are left over.

steps.text: This should print the total price. Fix line 2.
steps.hint: You can't join text and a number with +. Use a comma, or str().
steps.explanation: Python cannot add text and a number. A comma prints both, or str() turns the number into text.

steps.text: A pizza has 8 slices and you eat 3. Print how many are left, using a calculation.
steps.hint: Subtract eaten from slices inside print().

lessons.title: Comparing things
lessons.objective: Use comparisons that answer True or False.

steps.text: Comparisons answer True or False. == checks if two things are equal.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: <= means "less than or equal to". 10 is equal to 10, so it is True.

steps.text: You can compare text too. Capital letters matter!
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: 12 is not 13 or more, so the answer is False.

steps.text: One = stores a value; two == compare. Fix line 2 so it compares.
steps.hint: Use == to compare.
steps.explanation: A single = is for storing values. Comparing needs ==.

steps.text: Print whether 7 is greater than 4 (it should print True).
steps.hint: Put a comparison with > inside print().

lessons.title: Making choices with if
lessons.objective: Run code only when a condition is True.

steps.text: if runs the indented lines only when the condition is True. Don't forget the colon!
What will this print?
steps.explanation: 45 is less than 50, so the else part runs.

steps.text: else runs when the if condition is False.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: 4 % 2 is 0, so the number is even.

steps.text: Line 2 is missing something at the end. Fix it.
steps.hint: Every if line ends with a colon :
steps.explanation: Python needs a colon at the end of an if line.

steps.text: Finish the program: if hour is less than 12, print Selamat pagi, otherwise print Selamat petang.
steps.hint: Use if hour < 12: and else:, with the prints indented.

lessons.title: More choices with elif
lessons.objective: Choose between more than two paths.

steps.text: elif means "else if": it is checked only when the conditions above were False.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: The first condition that is True wins: 120 > 110, so it prints Too fast.

steps.text: and needs both sides True. or needs at least one.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: x is neither more nor less than 0, so the else part runs.

steps.text: Line 4 should be elif. Fix it.
steps.hint: else cannot have a condition; use elif.
steps.explanation: Only elif can have its own condition. else takes no condition.

steps.text: Finish the program to print Hot above 30, Warm above 20, and Cool otherwise.
steps.hint: Use if, elif and else in that order.

lessons.title: Loops with for
lessons.objective: Repeat code with for and range().

steps.text: A for loop repeats the indented lines. range(3) gives 0, 1, 2.
steps.code:
for i in range(3):
    print("Hip hip hooray!")
steps.expected_output:
Hip hip hooray!
Hip hip hooray!
Hip hip hooray!

steps.text: What will this print?
steps.code:
count = 0
for i in range(4):
    count = count + 1
print(count)
steps.explanation: range(4) gives 0, 1, 2 and 3, so the loop runs four times and count ends at 4.

steps.text: range(1, 4) starts at 1 and stops before 4.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.code:
for i in range(1, 4):
    print("Level", i)
steps.explanation: i takes the values 1, 2 and 3.

steps.text: Line 1 is missing something at the end. Fix it.
steps.hint: A for line ends with a colon : just like an if line.
steps.explanation: Python needs a colon at the end of a for line, before the indented lines.

steps.text: Use a for loop to print Hello 3 times.
steps.hint: for i in range(3): then an indented print.

lessons.title: Loops with while
lessons.objective: Repeat while a condition stays True.

steps.text: while repeats as long as its condition is True. Change the counter, or it never stops!
steps.code:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print(count)
    count = count + 1

steps.text: What will this print?
steps.code:
n = 10
while n > 0:
    n = n - 4
print(n)
steps.explanation: n goes 10, 6, 2, -2. Now n > 0 is False, so the loop stops and -2 is printed.

steps.text: A loop can add things up. This is called a running total.
steps.code:
total = 0
n = 1
while n <= 4:
    total = total + n
    n = n + 1
print(total)

steps.text: Type exactly what this prints.
steps.code:
x = 1
while x < 20:
    x = x * 3
print(x)
steps.explanation: x becomes 3, then 9, then 27. 27 is not below 20, so the loop stops.

steps.text: This loop never ends. Fix line 4 so the counter goes up.
steps.code:
i = 0
while i < 3:
    print("Go")
    i = i
steps.hint: The counter must change each time round.
steps.explanation: i never changed, so i < 3 stayed True forever. Adding 1 lets the loop finish.

steps.text: Use a while loop to print 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 (one per line).
steps.solution:
n = 5
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n = n - 1
steps.hint: Keep going while n > 0, and take 1 away from n each time.

lessons.title: Lists
lessons.objective: Keep many values in one list.

steps.text: A list holds many values in square brackets. Positions start at 0!
What will this print?
steps.explanation: Positions start at 0, so [1] is the second item: green.

steps.text: append() adds an item to the end of a list.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: nums[2] is 15 and nums[0] is 4, so the sum is 19.

steps.text: This list has 3 items, so the last position is 2. Fix line 2.
steps.hint: The last position is one less than the length.
steps.explanation: There is no position 3: the positions are 0, 1 and 2.

steps.text: Add "teh tarik" to the drinks list, then print the list.
steps.hint: Use drinks.append(...) and then print(drinks).

lessons.title: Looping through lists
lessons.objective: Visit every item in a list with a loop.

steps.text: for can visit every item in a list, one at a time.
steps.expected_output:
I love Ipoh
I love Kuching
I love Johor Bahru

steps.text: What will this print?
steps.code:
scores = [3, 5, 2]
total = 0
for s in scores:
    total = total + s
print(total)
steps.explanation: The loop adds every score: 3 + 5 + 2 = 10.

steps.text: Combine a loop and if to pick out some items.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: len() gives each word's length: hi is 2, hello is 5, hey is 3.

steps.text: Line 3 should add each price to the total. Fix it.
steps.code:
prices = [2, 3, 5]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total = p
print(total)
steps.hint: Add p to what total already has.
steps.explanation: total = p throws away the old total. total = total + p keeps adding.

steps.text: Print every number in the list doubled (one per line).
steps.hint: Loop over nums and print n * 2.
